zh.CATEGORY: AI 会议记录 / 会议智能（AI Meeting Notetakers）
zh.ONE_LINER_2_LINE_SUBTITLE: 它卖的不是「转写」，是「会开完，纪要和下一步已经在那儿」；免费档厚到不像免费，是它最锋利的获客武器，也是最脆的变现梁。
zh.USER_SCALE: 可核实：官网自述 Used at 500K+ companies（公司数口径，按官网原文，不是用户数）；Product Hunt 产品页 316 条评论（本次只抓到汇总计数与 8 条最新原话）；G2 4.6 分 / 177 条，但该页主体是另一个同名财务分析产品（详见评论证据）。官方未披露 ARR、付费席位数与留存，本卡不编。官网另有三个自述数字（95% 用户称能全程在场、每人每周省 6+ 小时跟进、洞察到行动快 3X），均为厂商口径，无第三方核实。
zh.STAGE_MATURITY: 成长期偏成熟，且已并入更大的套件。产品面三块：个人（bot 或 bot-free 采集、无限转写、即时摘要、clips 与播放列表、跨通话搜索；付费加高级摘要、AI 行动项、对话式助手、自定义 bot）、团队（共享工作区、Trackers、团队级 Ask Fathom、团队安全控制、标准 BAA 的 HIPAA）、企业（Launch Assist 实施、SSO 与 SCIM、自定义留存、可申请自定义 BAA、优先 SLA、专属成功经理）。跨端有 iOS App、桌面端与浏览器扩展。2026-04-15 Superhuman 官方公告宣布收购 Fathom。
zh.BUSINESS_MODEL_SHORT: 个人订阅 + 团队按席位订阅 + 合规档加价。个人 Free 0 美元 / Premium 16 美元；团队 2 人起，Team 15 / Business 25 / Enterprise 35 美元每人每月，Enterprise 仅年付；全部档位年付省 25%+，均写 90 day guarantee（官网定价页原文）。
zh.VERDICT_ONE_LINER: 它是会议的下游工厂：一段对话进去，纪要、行动项、跟进邮件出来。墙不在模型，而在「免费档太厚」与「平台原生免费捆绑」之间。
zh.VERDICT_BODY_2_3_LINES: 按拔电测试判为原生型：拿走 ASR 与摘要，它只剩音频文件（实测判定：一半是记录，一半是 AI 识别与上下文判断）。所以它的门槛不写在界面上，写在语言识别与采集入口上——实测三问的原话就是「门槛在语言识别准确度」。它真正站住的三件事是免费档、bot-free 和跨会议检索（Ask Fathom / MCP）；而这三件都能被平台方用「开会时本来就在那儿」的免费能力盖掉。
zh.TLDR_1_BODY: 无限录制、无限转写、即时摘要都在 0 美元档（定价页原文）。评论里至少两条独立原话在说这件事：一条写 I was actually confused with the features that they offered me for free，另一条写几乎担心他们给太多、试用期一到会不会收走。同一份定价页上，个人升级到 Premium 只买到高级摘要、AI 行动项、对话式助手与自定义 bot——也就是说，个人用户几乎感受不到那 16 美元的必要性。
zh.TLDR_2_BODY: 实测（燃冰）三问的结论是：值这个价（省的是记录时间，而记录在免费档就免费），门槛在模型这一侧，具体是语言识别准确度。这与 009 Figma（门槛在软件）正好互为镜像。摘要文本谁都能写像，能不能把多人抢话、口音、专业词写对，才是这个品类的地基。
zh.TLDR_3_HEADLINE: 最脆的梁有三根：免费太强、平台原生、定价权已不在自己手里
zh.TLDR_3_BODY: 第一根：评论里已经出现「Pro 试用两周后降回免费、价值大幅下降」的案例。第二根：官网自己列的对手里有 Google Meet 的 Gemini 与 ZoomMate，平台方开会时本来就在场，边际成本为零。第三根：2026-04-15 起它归属 Superhuman（官网首页横幅：FATHOM IS NOW PART OF SUPERHUMAN），独立定价权不再完全由自己掌握。
zh.SNAPSHOT_ONE_TO_TWO_SENTENCE_DEFINITION: Fathom 是一个 AI 会议记录与会议智能产品：用 bot 或 bot-free 方式采集会议音频，产出转写、摘要、行动项与跟进邮件，再把结果推进 CRM、Slack、Notion、Asana，或经 Public API 与 MCP 交给 ChatGPT、Claude 查询。
zh.USER_PROMISE: 官方一句话（官网原文）：Fathom summarizes your meetings so you can focus on the conversation。翻成用户语言：开会时不用记笔记，会开完纪要、行动项、跟进邮件已经在那儿。
zh.SEGMENT_1_NAME: 个人重度开会者（销售、教练、顾问、招聘）
zh.SEGMENT_1_DETAIL: 一周十几场会、会后还要写纪要的人。实测（燃冰）就落在这一层：原来人工整理至少半小时，现在会议中就能记录反馈。评论里的证据密度也在这层——一位创始人写自己一周 10+ 场客户通话，bot-free 让会里不再有人问「还有别人加入吗」。
zh.SEGMENT_2_DETAIL: 要的不是纪要，是「共享的客户事实来源」：Trackers 盯关键话题、Ask Fathom 跨通话检索、CRM 字段自动同步、Deal View 与 AI Scorecards 做教练。这些能力全部卡在团队档（Team 起），个人档拿不到——这是它主要的人格化付费理由。
zh.SEGMENT_3_DETAIL: 看的是 SSO 与 SCIM、自定义数据留存、可申请的 BAA、优先 SLA 与专属成功经理（Enterprise 档，仅年付），官网标 SOC 2 Type II / GDPR / HIPAA Compliant。这一层的钱包最厚，也最慢：采购周期长，但一旦进来，换的成本最高。
zh.JTBD_FUNCTIONAL: 把一场会变成能直接用的三样东西：可检索的转写、能读的摘要、能派活的行动项。
zh.JTBD_EMOTIONAL: 开会时敢不记笔记，也不怕漏掉对方承诺的那句话——实测原话是「人在会议上可以专注，不用再记录」。
zh.JTBD_SOCIAL: 在团队里成为「会开完就有结论」的那个人；在客户面前不必低头打字。
zh.TRIGGER_MOMENT: 一天里第三场会刚结束，邮箱里还躺着上一场的跟进没写。实测（燃冰）的触发点更简单：看到 landing page 上它展示的能力，决定试一下。
zh.FREQUENCY: 按会议频率走，重度用户每天数场；官方未披露使用频次数据。
zh.USAGE_CONTEXT: 会议软件里（Meet / Zoom / Teams）出发，落到网页或桌面端看摘要；行动项与纪要走 Slack、Notion、Asana、邮件；数据出口是 CRM 与 API/MCP；移动端有 iOS App。
zh.LOOP_TRIGGER_DETAIL: 触发点不是「我要用 AI」，而是「这场会我得留个记录、还得派活」。实测（燃冰）记录的第一印象是：它有两部分，一部分是会议记录，一部分是 AI 识别和上下文判断。
zh.LOOP_ACTION_TITLE: 让它进会，或者干脆不请机器人
zh.LOOP_ACTION_DETAIL: 实测流程：先在 landing page 注册，逐步授权会议相关邮箱与会议工具，最后一步才下载安装（安装是浏览器方式打开，也支持插件）。这一步是全流程里唯一需要停下来想的：先交权限，后见产品。
zh.LOOP_REWARD_TITLE: 摘要 + 行动项 + 下一步，直接能看
zh.LOOP_REWARD_DETAIL: 实测结论：能直接用；要改只改「会议共识和行动清单」这类内容，不改格式。最像智能的一刻是它把下一步行动提炼出来、再让人确认。
zh.LOOP_RETURN_TITLE: 历史会议沉下来，下次直接搜
zh.LOOP_RETURN_DETAIL: 回来的理由不是「再记一次」，而是「上次那场会他说了什么」。Trackers 与 Ask Fathom 让历史会议变成可查询的资产，团队档还多一层共享工作区。
zh.LOOP_FREQ: 每场会一次；重度用户每天 3–8 次（[推断] 依据：会议密度与官网 Solutions 的岗位切分，官方未披露频次）。
zh.LOOP_FREQ_NOTE_TRIGGER_CONTEXT: 同一个触发反复出现：会一结束就要有纪要。它把这一步从「人回忆着写」改成「机器已经写好、人来确认」。
zh.LOOP_ONE_LINE_INSIGHT_WHAT_THE_LOOP_ACTU: 它真正教用户的是「会议的价值不在记录，在会后的行动」——用过一次之后，人会开始按行动项开会，而不是按议程开会。
zh.ACQUISITION_LOOP_DETAIL: 三条同时跑：一是免费档口碑（无限录制让「先试试」没有成本，评论里多人在说免费档就够用）；二是内容与 SEO 矩阵——官网 Competitors 导航下每个对手都有一张对比页，专吃「X vs Fathom」的搜索；三是集成目录与生态（Salesforce、HubSpot、Slack、Asana、Zapier、ChatGPT、Claude），在别人的市场里被搜到。
zh.AHA_MOMENT_DETAIL: 第一次会开完，摘要、行动项、跟进邮件已经在页面上，而且会里没有第三方机器人。评论原话：removes the awkward "is someone else joining?" moment that always derailed the first 30 seconds。
zh.VIRALITY_DETAIL_OR_NONE: 有，但弱，而且 bot-free 与病毒传播天然反向：bot 进会是最显眼的品牌露出，偏偏它把这一项当成缺点来消除。真正带传播的是「把纪要链接发给没装的人看」——推断，官网未披露分享数据。
zh.RETENTION_1: 历史会议沉在账号里：转写、摘要、行动项都能搜，迁移等于放弃自己的会议档案。
zh.RETENTION_2: 团队档的共享工作区与 Trackers 一旦被用来盯指标（竞品提及、流失原因），就成了管理流程的一部分。
zh.RETENTION_3: CRM 字段自动回写把「会」和「客户记录」缝在一起，拔掉它等于回到手抄。
zh.GROWTH_LOOP_1_DETAIL: 个人免费无限录制 → 用顺了带进团队 → 团队要共享工作区与合规 → 买席位。这条环的强度全押在「免费档够用」上，所以它既是增长引擎，也是转化漏斗的漏点。
zh.GROWTH_LOOP_2_DETAIL: 官网 Competitors 下每个对手一张对比页（Fireflies、Granola、Gong、Otter、Read AI、ZoomMate、Google Meet 的 Gemini）→ 搜索「某工具 vs Fathom」的人落地 → 直接进免费档。这是典型的高意图 SEO，成本低、周期长。
zh.SURFACE_1_ROLE: 产品的入口，也是它的护城河所在：bot 入会最通用，bot-free 用桌面端抓系统音频，解决「会议里有机器人很尴尬」这件事（官网原话：Now available bot-free）。
zh.SURFACE_2_ROLE: 产品的主菜。实测看到的是摘要、视频与待办同屏；行动项由 AI 提炼、人确认——这个「AI 干活、人签字」的结构，是它最正确的设计。
zh.SURFACE_3_ROLE: 把单场会变成数据库：跨会议检索、按话题追问。团队档的 Ask Fathom 是「问整个团队的会」，这是从记录工具走向记忆层的分界线。
zh.SURFACE_4_ROLE: 让 AI 不只事后总结，还事前盯着：竞品提及、定价异议、流失原因这类话题可被自动标记。这是销售管理者最愿意付钱的一层。
zh.SURFACE_5_NAME: 集成与出口（CRM / Slack / API / MCP）
zh.SURFACE_5_ROLE: 会议结果必须有去处，否则就是又一个孤岛。Business 档的 CRM 字段同步与 Deal View，加上 Public API 与 MCP（接 ChatGPT、Claude），决定了它是「一个工具」还是「一层数据」。
zh.SURFACE_6_ROLE: 钱与合规都在这一层：2 人起、按席位、Business 与 Enterprise 之间隔着 CRM 同步、SSO/SCIM 与自定义留存。定价页的档位切分比功能本身更能说明它的商业意图。
zh.ENTITY_1: Meeting（一场会，采集与产出的最小单位）
zh.ENTITY_3: Summary / Action Item（摘要与行动项，真正被消费的东西）
zh.ENTITY_5: Workspace / Seat（团队与席位，钱和权限的边界）
zh.IA_LOGIC_PARAGRAPH: 主轴是「会议」：日历或会议软件里进来，落到一场一场的记录上，再横向串成搜索与 Trackers。这个结构的好处是用户不需要学任何新概念——会议本来就是他生活里的单位；代价是产品没有自己的「画布」，所有价值都寄存在别人的会议软件里，采集权限一断，产品就空。
zh.NAV_INTERACTION_PARAGRAPH: 实测（燃冰）的路径是：landing page 先看懂它能干什么 → 注册 → 逐步授权邮箱与会议工具 → 最后下载安装（浏览器方式打开，支持插件）。界面本身没有学习成本，卡点在授权这一段：用户要先交出会议入口，才能看到产品。这个顺序对增长有利（先建账号再建体验），对信任是考验。
zh.CRAFT_1_NAME: 先授权、后下载的入门顺序
zh.CRAFT_1_DETAIL: 实测最值得记的一处工艺：它不让你先装个用不上的客户端，而是把注册与授权拆成几步，最后一步才下载。结果是用户第一次打开产品时，会议已经在里面了——第一次体验就是「有结果」，不是「空界面」。
zh.CRAFT_2_NAME: 把「机器人进会」当成缺点来消除
zh.CRAFT_2_DETAIL: bot-free 不只是技术选项，是社交设计：会里没有第三方机器人，就没有开场那 30 秒的尴尬（评论原话点名）。愿意为一个「别人看不见我」的采集方式做桌面端，说明它理解这个品类的真实摩擦不在功能表上。
zh.CRAFT_3_NAME: 行动项：AI 提炼，人确认
zh.CRAFT_3_DETAIL: 实测原话：会议的下一步行动她也会提炼然后让人确认。这是把「不可逆的对外承诺」留在人手里的正确做法——AI 只做草稿，签字权不交出去。
zh.CRAFT_4_NAME: 免费档用「无限」而不是「限量」
zh.CRAFT_4_DETAIL: 大多数工具用分钟数设墙，它用功能设墙：录制与转写无限，付费买的是高级摘要、团队协作与合规。这个选择的代价是转化压力全压在团队档，好处是口碑极其干净——316 条评论里抱怨只有 10 条。
zh.CRAFT_5_NAME: 把会议做成可被别的 AI 调用的数据源
zh.CRAFT_5_DETAIL: Public API 与 MCP（ChatGPT、Claude）意味着它不争「谁来当助手」，而是争「助手读谁的会议记录」。评论里已经有人在等这条：希望能跨全部销售对话查询，而不是复制粘贴转写稿。
zh.CRAFT_PRINCIPLE: 先把「会中零摩擦」做到极致，再谈 AI 写得多好。它所有的工艺选择都在减少会议当场的那点不适，而不是增加会后的功能按钮。
zh.TTV_LABEL: 价值到达时间：本次未测（实测未计时，只记录了流程顺序：注册 → 授权 → 下载 → 进会 → 出摘要）
zh.TTV_NOTE_WHAT_HAPPENS_AT_AHA: 实测（燃冰）记录的是结果不是秒表：会开完，摘要与行动项已经在那儿，且可以直接用。本报告不把这一步换算成分钟，也不编评分。
zh.COG_LABEL: 认知负荷：低（landing page 就能看懂它干什么；真正的卡点是授权，不是界面）
zh.DELIGHT_1: 会里没有机器人（bot-free），开场不用解释「它是什么」（评论原话点名的尴尬被消掉了）。
zh.DELIGHT_2: 免费档无限录制与无限转写，试用没有额度焦虑（定价页原文；实测结论：免费就很强大，还给了丰富的 API 与 AI 接入）。
zh.DELIGHT_3: 行动项被提炼出来让人确认，而不是丢一段摘要让人自己找活（实测原话）。
zh.DELIGHT_LABEL: 惊喜点：零社交摩擦的采集 + 无额度焦虑的免费 + 会后就有的行动项
zh.TRUST_LABEL: 信任：产品层很稳（PH 316 条评论仅 10 条抱怨），合规标识齐全（SOC 2 Type II / GDPR / HIPAA，团队档含标准 BAA）；但实测的判断是「错不起」——纪要错一个承诺，下游全歪。
zh.STRUGGLE_1: 中文多人抢话的识别不稳：实测认定的门槛就在语言识别准确度，识别一歪，摘要与行动项全歪。
zh.STRUGGLE_2: 免费太强导致「为什么升级」说不清：评论里有 Pro 试用两周后降回免费、价值大幅下降的案例，也有人抱怨它想加入所有通话而自己拿不到价值。
zh.STRUGGLE_3: 手机与电话场景没闭环：评论 Cons 里 no mobile app 出现 3 次，原话希望接原生 iPhone 通话或至少方便上传电话录音。
zh.STRUGGLE_LABEL: 摩擦：中文识别、升级理由、移动与电话场景
zh.REVENUE_MODEL_NAME: 个人订阅 + 团队席位 + 合规档
zh.REVENUE_MODEL_DETAIL: 个人 Free 0 / Premium 16 美元；团队 2 人起，Team 15 / Business 25 / Enterprise 35 美元每人每月（Enterprise 仅年付）。合规与实施能力（SSO/SCIM、自定义留存、自定义 BAA、Launch Assist、专属成功经理）集中在最高档，是典型的「越往上越像企业软件」的定价结构。
zh.MON_ENTRY_HEADLINE: 入口免费到不像话，钱收在团队与合规上
zh.MON_ENTRY_DETAIL: Free 档给无限录制与无限转写，等于把「试用」这件事从流程里删掉；一旦要共享工作区、Trackers、团队级问答与 BAA，就跨进 Team 15 美元；要 CRM 同步与教练指标进 Business 25；要 SSO/SCIM 与自定义留存进 Enterprise 35（仅年付）。它卖的是「从个人工具变成团队基础设施」这一跳。
zh.FREE_PAID_DETAIL: 免费：无限录制与转写、即时摘要、clips 与播放列表、跨通话搜索、bot 或 bot-free 可选。付费：个人 16 美元买高级摘要、AI 行动项、对话式助手、自定义 bot；团队 15 美元起买共享工作区、Trackers、团队级 Ask Fathom、团队安全控制与标准 BAA 的 HIPAA；25 美元加 CRM 字段同步、Deal View、Coaching 指标与 AI Scorecards；35 美元加 Launch Assist、SSO 与 SCIM、自定义留存、自定义 BAA、优先 SLA。
zh.UX_MON_HEADLINE: 体验与变现是对齐的，还是打架的？
zh.UX_MON_DETAIL_ARE_THEY_ALIGNED_OR_IN_TEN: 结构上打架。对齐的一面：免费档解决「先试试」的心理成本，付费点落在团队协作与合规——这两样恰好是个人永远用不到、团队一定会撞上的东西，切得很准。打架的一面：个人层的免费档好用到评论里说「几乎担心他们给太多」，于是个人升级的理由只剩下高级摘要与 AI 行动项这种「可有可无的加强」；转化压力全部压到团队档，而团队档的采购决策者（经理、IT、合规）与最初的使用者（销售个人）不是同一个人。
zh.COMP_1_D1: 同一批人：会议多、要纪要的销售与团队
zh.COMP_1_D2: bot 入会为主，100+ 语言，AskFred 助手，私有存储
zh.COMP_1_D3: 会议软件市场与集成目录，自述 1,000,000+ companies
zh.COMP_1_D4: 官网公开四档：Free 0 / Pro 18（年付 10）/ Business 29（年付 19）/ Enterprise 39（仅年付），美元每人每月
zh.COMP_2_D1: 不想让机器人进会的个人与小组
zh.COMP_2_D2: 本地系统音频、无 bot，Mac 优先
zh.COMP_2_D3: 创始人/投资人圈子的口碑传播
zh.COMP_2_D4: 定价页为 JS 渲染，本次未读到可引用的价格原文（不编）
zh.COMP_3_D1: 会议 + 录音笔双场景的通用用户
zh.COMP_3_D2: 自研 ASR 起家，OtterPilot 自动入会
zh.COMP_3_D3: 教育与企业长尾，多年品牌积累
zh.COMP_3_D4: 定价页本次只读到学生折扣 FAQ 段（Pro 年付 79.99 美元学生价），正价未完整读取
zh.COMP_4_NAME: 平台原生（Google Meet 的 Gemini / Teams 的 Copilot / Zoom AI Companion）
zh.COMP_4_D1: 所有已经在用这个会议软件的人
zh.COMP_4_D2: 长在会议软件里，不需要采集权限
zh.COMP_4_D3: 会议软件的默认位置，零分发成本
zh.COMP_4_D4: 随会议软件订阅捆绑或加购，用户感知为「本来就有」
zh.COMP_OWN_D1: AI 会议记录与会议智能
zh.COMP_OWN_D2: bot 或 bot-free 双采集 + 摘要/行动项 + Trackers + 跨会议检索 + CRM 同步 + API/MCP
zh.COMP_OWN_D3: 免费档口碑、七张竞品对比页的 SEO、集成目录
zh.COMP_OWN_D4: 官网明码标价：个人 0/16，团队 15/25/35，年付省 25%+，90 天保证
zh.COMP_INTRO: 名单取自四处：官网 Competitors 导航（Fireflies、Granola、Gong、Otter、Read AI、ZoomMate、Google Meet 的 Gemini、内置方案）、官方 Solutions 里正面撞上的销售智能层（Gong）、以及评论里用户提到的替代对象（Fireflies、Zoom 与 Google Meet 原生）。Product Hunt 产品页本次被 Cloudflare 拦截，未取到 More alternatives 一栏，**所以不拿 PH 的相似产品清单充数**。
zh.COMP_WHERE_OWN_WINS: 三处别人短期不好补：一是免费档的厚度（无限录制与转写，直接消掉试用心理成本）；二是 bot-free 的采集方式（Granola 在做，但生态与集成远不如它）；三是跨会议检索加 MCP 出口——让 Claude、ChatGPT 直接读它的会议记录，等于把自己塞进别人的 AI 工作流。
zh.COMP_WHERE_RIVALS_CATCH: 三条缝：平台原生（Gemini / Copilot 开会时本来就在，用户不会为同一件事再买一份）；Fireflies 的价格与语言覆盖（年付 10 美元起、100+ 语言）；Gong 的销售管理深度（它往上打的 Business 档正好撞上 Gong 的主场）。中文市场则是第四道缝，实测的门槛结论已经指出来了。
zh.CHANNEL_1: 高意图 SEO：每个对手一张对比页（Competitors 导航下七个），吃「X vs Fathom」「Fathom alternative」这类搜索。
zh.CHANNEL_2: Product Hunt 与媒体波峰：产品页 316 条评论，2026-04-15 被 Superhuman 收购带来一轮行业报道。
zh.CHANNEL_3: 生态目录：Salesforce、HubSpot、Slack、Asana、Zapier、ChatGPT、Claude 的应用目录里都能被搜到，等于在别人的市场里摆摊。
zh.FRICTION_1_TITLE: 免费太强，升级理由要靠团队去凑
zh.FRICTION_1_BODY_WHY_IT_MATTERS: 评论里的原话：Pro 试用两周后降回免费，价值大幅下降，后来换去别家 note taker；另一条抱怨它想加入所有通话而自己拿不到价值。对一个 PLG 产品，这不是价格问题，是「个人永远不该付钱」的结构性问题——它把付费决策推给了团队，也就把增长曲线的斜率交给了别人。
zh.FRICTION_2_BODY: Google Meet 的 Gemini、Teams 的 Copilot、Zoom 的 AI Companion 都在做同一件事，且用户不用新开一个账号、不用授权、不用请机器人。官网把 Gemini 列进 Competitors，等于自己承认了这条威胁。
zh.FRICTION_3_TITLE: 中文与多人抢话的识别不稳
zh.FRICTION_3_BODY: 实测（燃冰）的结论直接落在这里：门槛在语言识别准确度。中文会议常见的抢话、方言口音、中英混说，是这类产品最容易露馅的地方；一旦转写失真，摘要与行动项会一起失真，而行动项指错方向比不写更贵。
zh.FRICTION_4_TITLE: 移动与电话场景没闭环
zh.FRICTION_4_BODY: 评论里 no mobile app 出现 3 次，原话希望接原生 iPhone 通话、或至少方便上传电话录音。对销售与顾问，很多关键对话发生在手机上，这段漏掉，会议档案就是残缺的。
zh.METRICS_INTRO: 官方未公开运营指标。以下分两类：能核实的公开事实（价格、评论数、评级分布），与标注 [推断] 的「它应该看什么」，不是真实数据。
zh.NORTH_STAR_METRIC: 每周被处理并产出行动项的会议数（[推断]）
zh.NORTH_STAR_WHY: [推断] 它按席位收费、按会议产出价值：会议数决定使用深度，行动项产出率决定「有没有真的被用起来」。北美星不该是注册数——免费档无限，注册数会虚高。
zh.INPUT_METRIC_1_NAME: 免费档 → 团队档的转化（按首次带人进工作区计）
zh.INPUT_METRIC_1_WHY: 个人层几乎不需要付费（实测：免费就很强），真正的收入跳变发生在「一个人把同事拉进共享工作区」那一刻。这个转化率才是它的生命线。
zh.INPUT_METRIC_2_NAME: 席位扩张速度（Team → Business → Enterprise）
zh.INPUT_METRIC_2_WHY: 价格从 15 到 25 到 35，跨度不大，但每跨一档都绑定一项新能力（CRM 同步、SSO/SCIM、自定义留存）。席位扩张速度说明它到底是「个人工具顺带团队用」还是「团队基础设施」。
zh.INPUT_METRIC_3_NAME: CRM 回写成功率与 Trackers 命中率
zh.INPUT_METRIC_3_WHY: Business 档卖的是闭环：会议结果要真的落进 CRM 字段、Trackers 要真的抓到竞品与异议。这两项失败，续费谈判会立刻变成「我们只把它当录音笔用」。
zh.GUARDRAIL_METRIC: 摘要被人工修改率 + 录音同意与合规投诉数
zh.GUARDRAIL_WHY: 实测的结论是「错不起」：纪要错一个承诺，下游全歪。修改率是识别质量最诚实的代理指标；而录音同意（各州/各国双 consent）是这个品类唯一可能致命的法律面。
zh.METRIC_BLINDSPOT: 没有公开的留存曲线、付费席位流失、单位 ASR 与推理成本 [推断]
zh.METRIC_BLINDSPOT_WHY: [推断] 免费档无限录制意味着免费用户也在持续烧 ASR 与推理成本；如果只看注册与评论，会看不见「免费越受欢迎、毛利越薄」。另一边，被收购后的整合度（是否并入 Superhuman 套件）不会体现在任何产品指标里，却决定它三年后的定价权。
zh.MOAT_REASONING_ONE_LINE: 免费档与 bot-free 8、集成与 MCP 7、团队工作流 6、品牌与分发 6、识别与模型 5、独立定价权 4（已被收购），加权 6：能被复制的是功能，难复制的是「个人先用顺、团队再买单」这条路径。
zh.HORIZONTAL_1: 从记录到行动：AI 行动项、跟进邮件、CRM 字段同步、Deal View——把会议末端接上销售流程。
zh.HORIZONTAL_2: 从单会到跨会：Trackers、Ask Fathom、AI Scorecards——把会议从「一场一场」变成「可查询的数据集」（[推断] 这是它唯一能躲开平台原生的方向）。
zh.VERTICAL_1: 销售与客户成功：客户通话、异议与竞品提及、续约风险。
zh.VERTICAL_2: 招聘、教练、咨询、运营：官网 Solutions 已按岗位切开六个，说明它在往「所有开会的人」铺。
zh.PLATFORM_1: 开放接口已存在：Public API 与 MCP（ChatGPT、Claude），加上 Zapier 与一堆原生集成。
zh.PLATFORM_2: [推断] 它的平台策略是「做别人的数据源」——不争助手入口，争会议记录这一层的事实权；被 Superhuman 收购后，最可能的走向是成为套件里的一项能力，而不是继续做独立超级 App。
zh.OPP_1_HEADLINE: （我的判断）把中文多人抢话做成第一等公民
zh.OPP_1_DETAIL_WHAT_HOW_WHY: 怎么做：把中文会议（抢话、口音、中英混说、专业词）做成独立的评测集与可选模型档，允许用户按会议类型切换识别策略。为什么：实测认定的门槛就在这里，而中文市场几乎只有会议软件自带的免费能力可用；谁能把这一段做稳，谁就拿走这块空白。
zh.OPP_2_HEADLINE: （我的判断）把「先授权、后下载」的入门顺序抄成模板
zh.OPP_2_DETAIL: 怎么做：注册 → 逐步授权 → 最后才装客户端，让第一次打开就有结果。为什么：实测最值得记的一处工艺；对任何「需要连接外部数据源才有价值」的 AI 产品，这个顺序都把「空界面」这一关删掉了。
zh.OPP_3_HEADLINE: （我的判断）把行动项做成带签字的审阅
zh.OPP_3_DETAIL: 怎么做：每条行动项标注来源时间戳与说话人，一键确认后才进 CRM 或发给客户，未确认的标为草稿。为什么：实测的兜底只有「人工确认」四个字，而这类产品错一次就可能把承诺写错；把签字这一步显式化，是把「错不起」变成「错不了」。
zh.STRATEGIC_HEADLINE: 它的赌注：用免费档占住个人，用团队与合规收钱，用 MCP 变成别人的数据源
zh.STRATEGIC_DETAIL_HIGH_IMPACT_BET: 三个动作叠在一起：免费档给到「个人不需要付费」的程度（换口碑与渗透）、团队档从共享工作区与 Trackers 起价（换 ARPU）、再用 API 与 MCP 把自己塞进 ChatGPT 与 Claude 的工作流（换存在感）。前两个是 PLG 的标准打法，第三个是它对「平台原生免费」的唯一反制——因为平台不会把会议记录开放给别家的 AI。代价是它必须一直赢在识别质量上，而这恰好是它最容易被追平的地方。
zh.MOONSHOT_HEADLINE: 终局：会议结束后，工作已经分配完毕
zh.MOONSHOT_DETAIL_WHY_IT_COULD_RESHAPE_THE: 如果它能把「会议 → 行动项 → 派活 → 追踪 → 复盘」全部自动闭合，那么会议记录这个品类就消失了，剩下的叫「会议执行系统」。距离不在摘要写得多好（这一层已经过剩），在两件事：一是识别与说话人分离要稳到可以无人复核，二是「谁有权代表公司对外承诺」这条授权链必须在产品里成立。实测已经指出后半段是瓶颈——AI 只能提炼，签字仍然归人。
zh.RISK_INTRO: 风险按「可能性 × 影响」排序，严重度是我的判断，不是公司披露。
zh.RISK_1_NAME: 平台原生免费能力吞掉品类
zh.RISK_1_MIT: 守住平台做不到的三件：跨会议检索、CRM 与工具链回写、API/MCP 开放。同时把中文等平台薄弱语种做实——平台原生只在主流语种上够用。
zh.RISK_2_NAME: 被收购后产品独立性与定价权变化
zh.RISK_2_MIT: 对用户而言，唯一可靠的缓解是保住数据出口（API 与导出）；对公司而言，要在整合期给出明确的免费档与定价承诺，否则「收购即涨价」的预期会先赶走团队客户。
zh.RISK_3_NAME: 中文与多语种识别不稳
zh.RISK_3_MIT: 按语种分开评估与选模型，给用户可见的识别置信度与逐句回听入口；识别没把握时明确标「待核对」，而不是给一段看起来很像的摘要。
zh.RISK_4_NAME: 免费档太强，付费转化长期偏弱
zh.RISK_4_MIT: 把付费墙从「功能」往「协作与治理」搬：共享工作区、审计、留存策略、CRM 双向同步——这些是个人永远用不到、组织一定会要的东西，也是评论里降级用户不会抱怨的那类价值。
zh.SHOT_1_CAPTION: Fathom 官网主视觉（OG 主图）：产品定位是 AI 会议记录，2026 年起首页标注已归属 Superhuman（取自 fathom.ai 官方主图）
zh.SHOT_2_CAPTION: 官网产品概览图一：会议摘要自动挂到通话上，摘要与会议内容同屏（取自 fathom.ai/product）
zh.SHOT_3_CAPTION: 官网产品概览图二：左侧摘要面板，右侧音频播放器与转写同步（取自 fathom.ai/product）
zh.SHOT_4_CAPTION: 官网产品概览图三：摘要模块下挂视频播放器，支持按时间点回看（取自 fathom.ai/product）
zh.SHOT_5_CAPTION: 会议发现视图：把多场会议列成一屏，可搜索、可筛选（取自 fathom.ai 官网截图）
zh.SHOT_6_CAPTION: 按日期分组的会议列表：昨天与今天的会议并排，是「会议库」这一层的日常入口（取自 fathom.ai 官网截图）
zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_1: Ask Fathom：跨会议问答已经具备「检索 + 汇总 + 给结论」的雏形，是它最接近 agent 的一面。
zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_2: Public API 与 MCP：让 Claude、ChatGPT 直接读会议记录，等于把「动手」这一步交给外部 agent，自己只保留事实源。
zh.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_3: [推断] Trackers + 行动项 + CRM 回写已经是一条完整的执行链，只差「替人派活」的授权；一旦补上，它就从记录工具变成会议执行系统。
zh.AI_DISRUPTION_RISK: 两条：一是平台原生把「会议记录」做成免费默认（Gemini、Copilot、AI Companion），品类空间被压扁；二是 ASR 与摘要的商品化，让「功能差异」很难维持溢价——真正剩下的差异只有采集方式、数据沉淀与集成深度。
zh.AI_OPPORTUNITY_1: （我的判断）中文与多语种的高准确识别加说话人分离，是它最该补、也最能拉开差距的一层。
zh.AI_OPPORTUNITY_2: （我的判断）把行动项做成带来源与签字的任务，并追踪到完成——从「会议记录」延伸到「会议执行」，这是唯一能提高客单价又不冒犯个人用户的方向。
zh.ASSUMPTIONS_ONE_PARAGRAPH_LIST_WHAT_IS_I: 可核实：官网定位与功能清单、bot-free 与合规标识、Used at 500K+ companies（官网原文）、定价五档金额与功能对照（美元原价）、2026-04-15 Superhuman 收购公告、Product Hunt 316 条评论的汇总计数与 8 条最新原话、G2 4.6/177 与评级分布、Fireflies 定价页四档原价、实测（燃冰）六维记录。推断并已标注：频次、北美星与输入/护栏指标、毛利与单位成本、被收购后的整合走向、竞品中的 Granola 与 Otter 价格（本次未读到可引用正文）。
zh.ASSUMPTION_1: [推断] Used at 500K+ companies 是「公司数」而非付费席位数，免费用户也计入；官网未给出用户数、付费数与留存，任何按此推算的 ARR 都不可信。
zh.ASSUMPTION_2: [推断] 付费主力是团队档而非个人档：依据是免费档已含无限录制与转写（定价页原文）+ 实测个人层免费够用 + 评论里 Pro 降级案例；因此它的增长曲线取决于「一个人什么时候把同事拉进来」。
zh.CATEGORY_POSITIONING_PARAGRAPH: 它站在两条货架的交叉口：一边是会议记录工具（Fireflies、Otter、Granola），一边是销售智能与收入智能（Gong）。位置上它偏记录侧但更靠行动与集成：比纯记录工具多 CRM 同步与 Scorecards，比 Gong 少了通话评分与销售方法的深度，比平台原生多跨会议检索与开放接口。
zh.CURRENT_AI_USAGE_PARAGRAPH: AI 出现在六处：ASR 转写（含说话人分离）、即时摘要、AI 行动项与跟进邮件、Trackers（持续盯关键话题）、Ask Fathom（跨会议问答）、AI Scorecards 与 CRM 字段抽取；对外还有 Public API 与 MCP 供其他 AI 调用。实测（燃冰）用到的只是最基础的一段——记录、摘要、行动项——就已经成立。
zh.FINAL_BREAKS: 要中文高准确率的重度会议场景（实测的门槛结论）；不许第三方进会的客户（bot 入会是 Cons 里唯一被点名的采集反感项）；要私有化部署或数据不出内网的行业；需要会议室硬件与线下拾音的企业。
zh.FINAL_MOAT_OR_LACK_THEREOF: 护城河是「弱到中」：真护城河只有三条，且都可被覆盖——免费档的厚度（可被补贴追平）、bot-free 的采集（Granola 已在做）、会议数据的沉淀与出口（平台方一旦开放导出就失效）。它真正的资产是「个人先用顺、团队再买单」这条路径与七张对比页的搜索卡位，而不是模型。
zh.FINAL_WINS: 免费档厚到消掉试用心理成本、bot-free 删掉会中社交摩擦、跨会议检索与 MCP 把自己变成别人的数据源、七张竞品对比页构成的高意图 SEO 矩阵。
zh.SIX_INTRO: 按应用层六个维度写：不看它有多少 AI 功能，看它替掉了哪一步、又把什么麻烦甩回来。证据：2026-11-19 的 20 分钟实测（燃冰）、官网与定价页原文、Product Hunt 与 G2 抓到的评论。
zh.AI_TYPE_REASON: 拔电测试：拿走 ASR 与摘要，剩下的只有音频与日历条目——能录不能读，产品立刻退化成录音笔。所以判为原生（AI-native），不是嵌入。但它是两段式的原生：记录壳 + AI 脑，判断权在 AI 那半边（实测原话：一部分是会议记录，一部分是 AI 识别和上下文决策判断）。
zh.SIX_1: 替掉的是「会后写纪要 + 发邮件备案」这一段：原来人做，至少半小时，而且会议内容没法直接转成行动；现在会中就记录，会后摘要与行动项已经在那儿（实测原话：以前都是人工的，现在会议中就能记录反馈，以前至少要花半小时）。成本从人工时间变成 0 美元起（免费档），所以实测的结论是「值」。
zh.SIX_2: 脏活它啃掉转写、摘要、行动项、跟进邮件与 CRM 回写；甩回一次——要你把常用的会议工具授权接进来（实测原话：她需要我补充接入我常用的会议工具），以及行动项要人确认。这道授权不是偷懒，是品类门槛：不接会议，就没有音频。
zh.SIX_3: 能直接用。实测原话：能直接用，需要改的是会议共识和行动清单这一块；团队场景里确实有人拿它直接对外发（她本身主推团队使用）。也就是说它交回的是可以签字的纪要，不是需要重排的草稿。
zh.SIX_4: 兜底薄：它只如实记录会议、按会议给结果，没有来源标注也没有置信度；给错前提它顺着走（实测原话：如果给它的前提是错的，她也顺着走，兜底靠人工确认）。真正兜底的只有人。
zh.SIX_5: 错不起。有历史记录、能回听（可撤回），但「一边谈话一边形成销售决策」的会，行动项写歪会把下游带歪，而且承诺已经说出口——不可逆（实测原话：这种一边谈话一边形成销售决策的，错不起）。
zh.SIX_6: 换得掉，但团队换不掉。实测原话：换得掉，用其他免费会议记录工具可以替代，但差在识别稳定性上；对时效与成交要求高的团队换不掉，而且免费版越用越好用。所以它的留存不是「离不开」，是「没必要走」。

en.ONE_LINER_2_LINE_SUBTITLE: It doesn't sell transcription. It sells 'the meeting ends and the summary plus next steps are already there.' Its free tier is so generous it looks like a mistake — the sharpest acquisition weapon, and the weakest revenue beam.
en.USER_SCALE: Verifiable: the site says 'Used at 500K+ companies' (companies, per the site's own wording, not users); 316 reviews on the Product Hunt listing (only the count and 8 latest review excerpts were captured this round); G2 4.6 / 177, but that page is dominated by a different, same-named financial-analysis product (see review evidence). ARR, paid seats and retention are not disclosed, so this card does not invent them. The site also claims 95% of users say they were fully present, 6+ hours of follow-up saved per person per week, and 3X faster insight-to-action — all vendor claims, unverified by a third party.
en.STAGE_MATURITY: Growth, leaning mature, and already folded into a larger suite. Three product layers: individual (bot or bot-free capture, unlimited recording and transcription, instant summaries, clips and playlists, cross-call search; paid adds advanced summaries, AI action items, a conversational assistant, custom bots), team (shared workspace, Trackers, team-wide Ask Fathom, team security controls, HIPAA with a standard BAA), enterprise (Launch Assist onboarding, SSO and SCIM, custom retention, custom BAA on request, priority SLA, dedicated success manager). Cross-platform via iOS app, desktop and browser extension. On 2026-04-15 Superhuman announced its acquisition of Fathom.
en.BUSINESS_MODEL_SHORT: Individual subscription + per-seat team subscription + compliance uplift. Individual: Free $0 / Premium $16. Teams start at 2 seats: Team $15 / Business $25 / Enterprise $35 per user per month, Enterprise annual only; every plan saves 25%+ annually and carries a 90-day guarantee (pricing page).
en.VERDICT_ONE_LINER: It is the factory downstream of every meeting: a conversation goes in, notes, action items and follow-up email come out. The wall isn't the model — it's the gap between a free tier this generous and free native capture inside the meeting apps.
en.VERDICT_BODY_2_3_LINES: The unplug test says AI-native: remove ASR and summarization and only an audio file remains (the hands-on verdict: half recorder, half AI recognition and context judgement). So the barrier isn't in the UI, it's in speech recognition and the capture entry point — the hands-on answer was literally 'the barrier is recognition accuracy'. What actually holds is the free tier, bot-free capture, and cross-meeting retrieval (Ask Fathom / MCP). All three can be covered by the platform vendors who are already inside the meeting for free.
en.TLDR_1_HEADLINE: The free tier is too generous to look free
en.TLDR_1_BODY: Unlimited recording, unlimited transcription and instant summaries sit on the $0 plan (pricing page). At least two independent reviews say so: one writes 'I was actually confused with the features that they offered me for free', another says they were almost worried Fathom gives too much and would claw it back after the trial. On the same page, the individual upgrade to Premium buys only advanced summaries, AI action items, the conversational assistant and custom bots — meaning an individual user barely feels why the $16 is necessary.
en.TLDR_2_HEADLINE: The barrier is recognition, not summarization
en.TLDR_2_BODY: The three-question hands-on verdict: worth the price (it saves recording time, and recording is already free), and the barrier sits on the model side — specifically recognition accuracy. This mirrors 009 Figma, where the barrier sits in the software. Anyone can write a plausible summary; getting overlapping speakers, accents and domain terms right is the floor this category stands on.
en.TLDR_3_HEADLINE: Three weak beams: free tier too strong, native competition, and pricing power no longer its own
en.TLDR_3_BODY: First: a review already documents someone dropping from the Pro trial back to free after two weeks because value fell off. Second: its own competitor list includes Google Meet's Gemini and ZoomMate — the platforms are already in the room at zero marginal cost. Third: since 2026-04-15 it belongs to Superhuman (site banner: FATHOM IS NOW PART OF SUPERHUMAN), so independent pricing power is no longer fully in its hands.
en.SNAPSHOT_ONE_TO_TWO_SENTENCE_DEFINITION: Fathom is an AI meeting recorder and meeting-intelligence product: it captures audio with a bot or bot-free, produces transcripts, summaries, action items and follow-up emails, then pushes results into CRM, Slack, Notion and Asana, or exposes them through a public API and MCP for ChatGPT and Claude.
en.USER_PROMISE: Official line (site): 'Fathom summarizes your meetings so you can focus on the conversation.' In user language: stop taking notes in the meeting; the notes, action items and follow-up email are already there when it ends.
en.SEGMENT_1_NAME: Heavy individual meeting takers (sales, coaching, consulting, recruiting)
en.SEGMENT_1_DETAIL: People with a dozen meetings a week who still owe someone notes. The hands-on test (RanBing) sits exactly here: notes used to take at least half an hour, now feedback is captured during the meeting. The review evidence clusters here too — one founder writes about 10+ customer calls a week and how bot-free removed the awkward 'is someone else joining?' moment.
en.SEGMENT_2_DETAIL: They don't want notes, they want a shared source of customer truth: Trackers on key topics, Ask Fathom across calls, CRM field sync, Deal View and AI Scorecards for coaching. All of it gates at Team and above; the individual plan never touches it — which is the main reason a person would ever pay.
en.SEGMENT_3_DETAIL: They buy SSO and SCIM, custom retention, BAA on request, priority SLA and a dedicated success manager (Enterprise, annual only). The site claims SOC 2 Type II, GDPR and HIPAA compliance. Thickest wallet, slowest cycle — but once in, the highest switching cost.
en.JTBD_FUNCTIONAL: Turn one meeting into three usable artifacts: a searchable transcript, a readable summary, an action list someone can be assigned.
en.JTBD_EMOTIONAL: Be allowed to stop taking notes — and not fear missing the one sentence the other side committed to. The hands-on line: 'you can stay present in the meeting instead of writing things down.'
en.JTBD_SOCIAL: Be the person whose meetings end with conclusions; never be the one typing while a client talks.
en.TRIGGER_MOMENT: The third meeting of the day just ended and last meeting's follow-up is still unsent. In the hands-on test the trigger was simpler: the landing page showed what it could do, so it got tried.
en.FREQUENCY: Tied to meeting volume — several times a day for heavy users. Frequency data is not disclosed.
en.USAGE_CONTEXT: Starts inside the meeting app (Meet / Zoom / Teams), lands on web or desktop for the summary; action items and notes flow to Slack, Notion, Asana, email; data exits through CRM, API and MCP; iOS app on mobile.
en.LOOP_TRIGGER_DETAIL: The trigger isn't 'I want AI', it's 'I need a record of this and I need to hand out work'. The first hands-on impression: it has two halves — meeting recording, and AI recognition plus context judgement.
en.LOOP_ACTION_TITLE: Let it into the meeting — or skip the bot entirely
en.LOOP_ACTION_DETAIL: Hands-on flow: sign up from the landing page, authorise the meeting-related mailbox and meeting tools step by step, and only download at the very end (install opens in the browser, extensions supported). That is the one moment the whole flow asks you to stop and think: permissions first, product second.
en.LOOP_REWARD_TITLE: Summary, action items and next step, ready to read
en.LOOP_REWARD_DETAIL: Hands-on verdict: directly usable; the only things needing edits are the meeting consensus and the action list — not the format. The smartest moment is when it extracts the next actions and asks a human to confirm.
en.LOOP_RETURN_TITLE: Meetings accumulate; next time you search them
en.LOOP_RETURN_DETAIL: You come back not to record again but to ask 'what did they say last time'. Trackers and Ask Fathom turn history into a queryable asset, plus a shared workspace on team plans.
en.LOOP_FREQ: Once per meeting; 3–8 times a day for heavy users ([inferred] from meeting density and the site's role-based solutions; frequency is not disclosed).
en.LOOP_FREQ_NOTE_TRIGGER_CONTEXT: The same trigger repeats: the meeting ends and notes are owed. It converts that step from 'a human reconstructs it' to 'the machine wrote it, the human confirms'.
en.LOOP_ONE_LINE_INSIGHT_WHAT_THE_LOOP_ACTU: What it actually teaches is that a meeting's value lives in post-meeting action, not in the record — after one use, people start running meetings around action items instead of agendas.
en.ACQUISITION_LOOP_DETAIL: Three run at once: free-tier word of mouth (unlimited recording makes 'just try it' cost nothing — several reviews say the free plan is enough); a content/SEO matrix, where every competitor in the site's Competitors menu has its own comparison page eating 'X vs Fathom' searches; and integration directories (Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack, Asana, Zapier, ChatGPT, Claude), which is renting shelf space in someone else's market.
en.AHA_MOMENT_DETAIL: The first time a meeting ends and the summary, action items and follow-up email are already on the page — with no third-party bot in the room. Review quote: it 'removes the awkward "is someone else joining?" moment that always derailed the first 30 seconds'.
en.VIRALITY_DETAIL_OR_NONE: Yes, but weak — and bot-free is structurally anti-viral: a bot in the room is the most visible brand impression, and Fathom eliminated it as a defect. What does spread is sharing a notes link with someone who has no account — [inferred]; sharing data is not disclosed.
en.RETENTION_1: Meetings accumulate in the account: transcripts, summaries and action items are all searchable, so leaving means abandoning your own meeting archive.
en.RETENTION_2: Once team Trackers are used to watch metrics (competitor mentions, churn reasons), the product becomes part of the management process.
en.RETENTION_3: Automatic CRM field write-back stitches meetings into customer records; removing it means going back to copy-paste.
en.GROWTH_LOOP_1_DETAIL: Free unlimited recording → get fluent → bring it into a team → the team needs a shared workspace and compliance → seats are bought. The whole loop leans on 'free is enough', which makes it both the growth engine and the leak in the funnel.
en.GROWTH_LOOP_2_DETAIL: One comparison page per rival (Fireflies, Granola, Gong, Otter, Read AI, ZoomMate, Google Meet's Gemini) → high-intent searchers land → straight into the free tier. Classic high-intent SEO: cheap to run, slow to compound.
en.SURFACE_1_ROLE: The entry point and the moat: a bot joins any meeting, while bot-free grabs system audio on the desktop — solving 'a robot in the room is awkward' (site: 'Now available bot-free').
en.SURFACE_2_ROLE: The main dish. The hands-on view shows summary, video and to-dos on one screen; action items are drafted by AI and confirmed by a human — the 'AI drafts, human signs' structure is its most correct design decision.
en.SURFACE_3_ROLE: Turns single meetings into a database: cross-meeting retrieval, topic-level follow-up questions. Team-level Ask Fathom queries the whole team's meetings — the dividing line between a recorder and a memory layer.
en.SURFACE_4_ROLE: AI that watches instead of only summarising: competitor mentions, pricing objections, churn reasons get flagged automatically. This is the layer sales managers pay for.
en.SURFACE_5_NAME: Integrations and exits (CRM / Slack / API / MCP)
en.SURFACE_5_ROLE: Meeting output needs somewhere to go or it's another silo. Business-tier CRM field sync and Deal View, plus the public API and MCP (ChatGPT, Claude), decide whether it is 'a tool' or 'a layer of data'.
en.SURFACE_6_ROLE: Money and compliance live here: 2-seat minimum, per-seat pricing, and the gaps between Business and Enterprise are CRM sync, SSO/SCIM and custom retention. The tier cut lines describe the business intent better than the feature list does.
en.ENTITY_1: Meeting (one call; the unit of capture and output)
en.ENTITY_3: Summary / Action item (what actually gets consumed)
en.ENTITY_5: Workspace / Seat (the boundary of money and permissions)
en.IA_LOGIC_PARAGRAPH: The spine is 'the meeting': enter from a calendar or meeting app, land on individual records, then string them sideways into search and Trackers. The upside is zero new concepts — a meeting is already the unit of the user's day. The cost is that the product has no canvas of its own: all value is stored inside someone else's meeting app, and if capture permissions break, the product is empty.
en.NAV_INTERACTION_PARAGRAPH: The hands-on path: understand it from the landing page → sign up → authorise mailbox and meeting tools step by step → download last (browser-based install, extensions supported). The UI itself asks nothing to learn; the friction is the authorisation stretch — you hand over the meeting entry point before you see the product. Good for growth (account before experience), a test of trust.
en.CRAFT_1_DETAIL: The most instructive craft detail from the hands-on test: it does not make you install a client you can't use yet. Signup and permissions are split into steps and the download comes last, so the first time you open the product the meetings are already inside. The first experience is 'there is a result', not 'an empty screen'.
en.CRAFT_2_NAME: Treating 'a bot in the room' as a defect to remove
en.CRAFT_2_DETAIL: Bot-free is social design, not a technical checkbox: no third-party robot means no awkward first 30 seconds (named in reviews). Choosing to build a desktop capture path just so 'nobody can see me recording' tells you it understands where the real friction lives.
en.CRAFT_3_NAME: Action items: AI drafts, human signs
en.CRAFT_3_DETAIL: Hands-on line: 'she extracts the next actions and then has a human confirm them.' That is the right way to keep irreversible external commitments in human hands — AI writes the draft, signing authority never leaves.
en.CRAFT_4_NAME: A free tier metered by features, not minutes
en.CRAFT_4_DETAIL: Most tools put a minute counter on the wall; Fathom pays for itself in features — recording and transcription unlimited, and money buys advanced summaries, team collaboration and compliance. The cost is that all conversion pressure lands on team plans; the benefit is remarkably clean word of mouth — only 10 complaints across 316 reviews.
en.CRAFT_5_NAME: Making meetings a data source other AIs can call
en.CRAFT_5_DETAIL: The public API and MCP (ChatGPT, Claude) mean it isn't fighting over 'who is the assistant' but over 'whose meeting records the assistant reads'. Reviewers are already waiting for this: they want to query across all sales conversations instead of pasting transcripts.
en.CRAFT_PRINCIPLE: Make in-meeting friction disappear first, then argue about how well AI writes. Every craft choice here reduces discomfort during the meeting rather than adding buttons after it.
en.TTV_LABEL: Time-to-value: not measured this round (the hands-on run recorded sequence, not a stopwatch: signup → permissions → download → join → summary)
en.TTV_NOTE_WHAT_HAPPENS_AT_AHA: What the hands-on run recorded is an outcome, not a timer: the meeting ends and the summary plus action items are already there and directly usable. This report does not convert that into minutes, and does not invent a score.
en.COG_LABEL: Cognitive load: low (the landing page explains itself; the real friction is authorisation, not the interface)
en.DELIGHT_1: No bot in the room (bot-free), so nobody has to explain what that thing is (the exact awkwardness named in reviews).
en.DELIGHT_2: Unlimited recording and transcription on free — no quota anxiety while trialling (pricing page; hands-on verdict: the free version is already powerful, and it ships a rich API and AI integrations).
en.DELIGHT_3: Action items are extracted and confirmed rather than buried in a wall of summary (hands-on line).
en.DELIGHT_LABEL: Delight: zero-social-friction capture + quota-free free tier + action items that exist the moment the meeting ends
en.TRUST_LABEL: Trust: product layer is solid (only 10 complaints out of 316 PH reviews) and compliance badges are all present (SOC 2 Type II / GDPR / HIPAA, standard BAA on team plans). But the hands-on judgement is 'you can't afford to be wrong' — one wrong commitment in the notes and everything downstream bends.
en.STRUGGLE_1: Chinese-language overlapping speech is unstable: the hands-on test puts the barrier exactly at recognition accuracy, and when recognition drifts, summaries and action items drift with it.
en.STRUGGLE_2: Free is so strong that 'why upgrade' is hard to answer: one review drops from the Pro trial back to free after two weeks saying value fell off; another complains it tries to join every call without delivering value.
en.STRUGGLE_3: Mobile and phone-call scenarios aren't closed: 'no mobile app' appears 3 times in Cons, with reviewers asking for native iPhone call capture or at least an easy way to upload call recordings.
en.STRUGGLE_LABEL: Friction: Chinese recognition, upgrade rationale, mobile and phone-call gap
en.REVENUE_MODEL_NAME: Individual subscription + team seats + compliance tier
en.REVENUE_MODEL_DETAIL: Individual Free $0 / Premium $16; teams from 2 seats at Team $15 / Business $25 / Enterprise $35 per user per month (Enterprise annual only). Compliance and implementation capabilities (SSO/SCIM, custom retention, custom BAA, Launch Assist, dedicated CSM) are stacked at the top — the classic 'the higher you go, the more it looks like enterprise software' curve.
en.MON_ENTRY_HEADLINE: The entry is absurdly free; the money is in teams and compliance
en.MON_ENTRY_DETAIL: The free plan hands out unlimited recording and transcription, deleting 'trial' from the workflow. The moment you need a shared workspace, Trackers, team-wide Q&A and a BAA, you cross into Team at $15; CRM sync and coaching metrics pull you to Business at $25; SSO/SCIM and custom retention pull you to Enterprise at $35 (annual only). What it sells is the jump from 'personal tool' to 'team infrastructure'.
en.FREE_PAID_DETAIL: Free: unlimited recording and transcription, instant summaries, clips and playlists, cross-call search, bot or bot-free capture. Paid: $16 individual buys advanced summaries, AI action items, the conversational assistant, custom bots; $15 teams buy a shared workspace, Trackers, team-wide Ask Fathom, team security controls and HIPAA with a standard BAA; $25 adds CRM field sync, Deal View, coaching metrics and AI Scorecards; $35 adds Launch Assist, SSO and SCIM, custom retention, custom BAA and priority SLA.
en.UX_MON_HEADLINE: Are experience and monetisation aligned, or fighting?
en.UX_MON_DETAIL_ARE_THEY_ALIGNED_OR_IN_TEN: Structurally fighting. Aligned: the free tier removes the psychological cost of trying, and the paywall lands on team collaboration and compliance — exactly what an individual never needs and a team always hits. Fighting: the individual tier is so good that reviews say they were 'almost concerned they're offering too much', leaving only nice-to-have upgrades (advanced summaries, AI action items) as the reason to pay. All conversion pressure moves to team plans, where the buyer (manager, IT, compliance) is not the person who fell in love with the product.

en.COMP_1_D2: Bot-first, 100+ languages, AskFred assistant, private storage
en.COMP_1_D3: Meeting-app marketplaces and integration directories; claims 1,000,000+ companies

en.COMP_2_D2: Local system audio, no bot, Mac-first

en.COMP_3_D3: Education and enterprise long tail, years of brand equity
en.COMP_3_D4: Only the student-discount FAQ was readable this round (Pro $79.99/yr student price); list price not fully captured

en.COMP_4_D1: Everyone already using that meeting app
en.COMP_4_D2: Built into the meeting app; needs no capture permission
en.COMP_4_D3: The default surface of the meeting app — zero distribution cost
en.COMP_4_D4: Bundled or add-on with the meeting subscription; users perceive it as 'already included'

en.COMP_OWN_D2: Dual capture (bot or bot-free) + summaries/action items + Trackers + cross-meeting retrieval + CRM sync + API/MCP
en.COMP_OWN_D3: Free-tier word of mouth, seven competitor comparison pages for SEO, integration directories
en.COMP_OWN_D4: Public pricing: individual 0/16, teams 15/25/35, 25%+ off annual, 90-day guarantee
en.COMP_INTRO: The list comes from four places: the site's own Competitors menu (Fireflies, Granola, Gong, Otter, Read AI, ZoomMate, Google Meet's Gemini, an in-house option), the sales-intelligence layer its Business tier collides with head-on (Gong), and the substitutes reviewers mention (Fireflies, Zoom and Google Meet native). The Product Hunt listing was blocked by Cloudflare this round, so the 'More alternatives' block was not captured — **and no PH similar-product list is substituted for it**.
en.COMP_WHERE_OWN_WINS: Three things rivals can't close quickly: how thick the free tier is (unlimited recording and transcription removes trial friction outright); bot-free capture (Granola does it, but without this ecosystem and integration depth); and cross-meeting retrieval plus an MCP exit — letting Claude and ChatGPT read its meeting records inserts it into someone else's AI workflow.
en.COMP_WHERE_RIVALS_CATCH: Three gaps: platform-native (Gemini / Copilot are already in the room; nobody buys the same thing twice); Fireflies' price and language coverage ($10 annual entry, 100+ languages); Gong's sales-management depth (its Business tier walks straight into Gong's home ground). Chinese-language markets are the fourth gap, and the hands-on verdict already points at it.
en.CHANNEL_1: High-intent SEO: one comparison page per rival (seven under Competitors), capturing 'X vs Fathom' and 'Fathom alternative' searches.
en.CHANNEL_2: Product Hunt and press peaks: 316 reviews on the listing, plus the 2026-04-15 Superhuman acquisition coverage.
en.CHANNEL_3: Ecosystem directories: listed inside Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack, Asana, Zapier, ChatGPT and Claude marketplaces — a stall in someone else's bazaar.
en.FRICTION_1_TITLE: Free is too good, so the upgrade case has to be built by teams
en.FRICTION_1_BODY_WHY_IT_MATTERS: One review: dropped from the Pro trial to free after two weeks because value fell off, later switched to another note taker; another complains it wanted to join every call without delivering value. For a PLG product this isn't a pricing complaint — it's structural: individuals should never pay, so the payment decision is pushed to teams, and the growth curve's slope is handed to someone else.
en.FRICTION_2_BODY: Google Meet's Gemini, Teams' Copilot and Zoom's AI Companion do the same job with no new account, no permissions, no bot. Listing Gemini under Competitors is Fathom admitting the threat itself.
en.FRICTION_3_BODY: The hands-on verdict lands squarely here: the barrier is recognition accuracy. Interruptions, accents and mixed Chinese-English are where this category shows its seams; once the transcript is wrong, summaries and action items go wrong together — and an action item pointing the wrong way costs more than no action item at all.
en.FRICTION_4_TITLE: Mobile and phone calls aren't closed
en.FRICTION_4_BODY: 'No mobile app' appears 3 times in Cons, with reviewers asking for native iPhone call capture or at least easy upload of call recordings. For salespeople and consultants, many decisive conversations happen on a phone — miss those and the meeting archive is incomplete.
en.METRICS_INTRO: No operating metrics are disclosed. What follows separates verifiable public facts (prices, review counts, rating distribution) from [inferred] 'what it should watch' — not real data.
en.NORTH_STAR_METRIC: Meetings processed into action items per week ([inferred])
en.NORTH_STAR_WHY: [inferred] It charges per seat and delivers per meeting: meeting volume sets depth of use, action-item yield sets whether it is actually adopted. North star shouldn't be signups — free is unlimited, so signups inflate.
en.INPUT_METRIC_1_NAME: Free → team conversion (measured by first colleague added to a workspace)
en.INPUT_METRIC_1_WHY: Individuals almost never need to pay (hands-on: free is already strong); the revenue step change happens the moment one person pulls a colleague into a shared workspace. That conversion rate is the lifeline.
en.INPUT_METRIC_2_WHY: Prices run 15 → 25 → 35, a narrow span, but each step is bound to a new capability (CRM sync, SSO/SCIM, custom retention). Expansion velocity shows whether this is 'a personal tool teams happen to use' or 'team infrastructure'.
en.INPUT_METRIC_3_NAME: CRM write-back success rate and Tracker hit rate
en.INPUT_METRIC_3_WHY: The Business tier sells a closed loop: results must actually land in CRM fields, Trackers must actually catch competitors and objections. When those fail, renewal talks collapse into 'we only use it as a voice recorder'.
en.GUARDRAIL_METRIC: Human edit rate on summaries + recording-consent and compliance complaints
en.GUARDRAIL_WHY: The hands-on verdict is 'you can't afford to be wrong': one wrong commitment in the notes and everything downstream bends. Edit rate is the most honest proxy for recognition quality; recording consent (two-party consent jurisdictions) is the one legally fatal surface in this category.
en.METRIC_BLINDSPOT: No public retention curve, paid-seat churn, or unit ASR/inference cost [inferred]
en.METRIC_BLINDSPOT_WHY: [inferred] Unlimited free recording means free users keep burning ASR and inference spend; watching only signups and reviews hides that 'the more popular free gets, the thinner the margin'. Separately, post-acquisition integration into Superhuman won't show in any product metric yet determines its pricing power in three years.
en.MOAT_REASONING_ONE_LINE: Free tier and bot-free 8, integrations and MCP 7, team workflows 6, brand and distribution 6, recognition/model 5, independent pricing power 4 (already acquired) — weighted 6: features can be copied, but 'individuals get fluent first, teams pay later' is harder to copy.
en.HORIZONTAL_1: From record to action: AI action items, follow-up email, CRM field sync, Deal View — wiring the end of the meeting into the sales process.
en.HORIZONTAL_2: From single meeting to cross-meeting: Trackers, Ask Fathom, AI Scorecards — turning meetings from events into a queryable dataset ([inferred] its only route around platform-native capture).
en.VERTICAL_1: Sales and customer success: customer calls, objections and competitor mentions, renewal risk.
en.VERTICAL_2: Recruiting, coaching, consulting, operations: the site's Solutions menu is already cut by role across six, showing the push toward 'everyone who meets'.
en.PLATFORM_1: Open interfaces already exist: public API and MCP (ChatGPT, Claude), plus Zapier and a long list of native integrations.
en.PLATFORM_2: [inferred] Its platform strategy is to be someone else's data source — not to win the assistant entry point but to own the factual layer of meeting records. Post-acquisition, the likeliest path is becoming a capability inside a suite rather than a standalone super-app.
en.OPP_1_HEADLINE: (My judgement) Make Chinese overlapping speech a first-class citizen
en.OPP_1_DETAIL_WHAT_HOW_WHY: How: treat Chinese meetings (interruptions, accents, mixed CN/EN, domain terms) as a separate evaluation set and a selectable model tier, letting users switch recognition strategy by meeting type. Why: that is exactly where the hands-on test found the barrier, and the Chinese market currently has almost nothing but free native capture — whoever stabilises this takes the gap.
en.OPP_2_HEADLINE: (My judgement) Copy the 'authorise first, download last' onboarding as a template
en.OPP_2_DETAIL: How: signup → stepwise permissions → install the client only at the end, so the first launch already shows results. Why: it was the most instructive craft detail in the hands-on run; for any AI product that only becomes valuable once it connects an external data source, this order deletes the 'empty screen' moment.
en.OPP_3_HEADLINE: (My judgement) Make action items a signed review step
en.OPP_3_DETAIL: How: every action item carries its source timestamp and speaker; nothing enters the CRM or goes to a client until one click confirms it, and unconfirmed items stay marked as drafts. Why: the only safety net in the hands-on test was the phrase 'human confirmation', and one wrong commitment can be fatal — making the signature explicit turns 'can't afford to be wrong' into 'can't be wrong'.
en.STRATEGIC_HEADLINE: Its bet: free tier owns the individual, teams and compliance pay, MCP makes it someone else's data source
en.STRATEGIC_DETAIL_HIGH_IMPACT_BET: Three moves stacked: a free tier generous enough that individuals never need to pay (buying word of mouth and penetration), team tiers starting at shared workspace and Trackers (buying ARPU), and API/MCP to insert itself into ChatGPT's and Claude's workflows (buying relevance). The first two are standard PLG; the third is its only counter to free native capture — because platforms will never hand their meeting records to someone else's AI. The price is that it must keep winning on recognition quality, which is precisely where it is easiest to catch up.
en.MOONSHOT_HEADLINE: Endgame: when the meeting ends, the work is already assigned
en.MOONSHOT_DETAIL_WHY_IT_COULD_RESHAPE_THE: If it can close the loop from meeting → action item → assignment → tracking → review, the 'meeting notetaker' category dissolves and what remains is a meeting execution system. The distance is not summary quality (that layer is already oversupplied) but two things: recognition and diarisation stable enough to skip human review, and an authorisation chain that answers 'who may commit the company externally'. The hands-on test already found the second one is the bottleneck — AI can only draft; signing still belongs to a person.
en.RISK_INTRO: Risks ordered by likelihood × impact; severity is my judgement, not a company disclosure.
en.RISK_1_NAME: Native free capability swallows the category
en.RISK_1_MIT: Hold the three things platforms won't do: cross-meeting retrieval, CRM and toolchain write-back, open API/MCP. And make weak-language markets (Chinese) genuinely good — native tools are only adequate in major languages.
en.RISK_2_MIT: For users, the only reliable hedge is a data exit (API and export). For the company, integration periods need explicit free-tier and pricing commitments — otherwise the 'acquired means more expensive' expectation drives team customers out before any change lands.
en.RISK_3_MIT: Evaluate and select models per language, show visible confidence and per-sentence replay; when recognition is shaky, label it 'needs checking' instead of producing a plausible-looking summary.
en.RISK_4_NAME: Free tier too strong, conversion structurally weak
en.RISK_4_MIT: Move the paywall from features to collaboration and governance: shared workspaces, audit, retention policy, two-way CRM sync — things an individual never needs, an organisation always demands, and downgraders in reviews never complain about.

en.SHOT_2_CAPTION: Product overview 1: the meeting summary is attached to the call, summary and content on one screen (from fathom.ai/product)
en.SHOT_3_CAPTION: Product overview 2: summary panel on the left, audio player synced with the transcript on the right (from fathom.ai/product)
en.SHOT_4_CAPTION: Product overview 3: a video player under the summary block, jump back to any timestamp (from fathom.ai/product)
en.SHOT_5_CAPTION: Meeting discovery view: many meetings on one screen, searchable and filterable (from fathom.ai)

en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_1: Ask Fathom: cross-meeting Q&A already shows the retrieve-summarise-conclude shape — the most agent-like surface it has.
en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_2: Public API and MCP: letting Claude and ChatGPT read meeting records hands the 'act' step to an external agent while keeping the source of truth.
en.AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_3: [inferred] Trackers + action items + CRM write-back is already a complete execution chain; only the authority to assign work on someone's behalf is missing. Add that and it moves from recorder to meeting execution system.
en.AI_DISRUPTION_RISK: Two: platform-native makes meeting notes a free default (Gemini, Copilot, AI Companion), flattening the category; and commoditised ASR and summarisation make feature differences hard to price. What's left as differentiation is capture method, data accumulation and integration depth.
en.AI_OPPORTUNITY_1: (My judgement) High-accuracy Chinese and multilingual recognition with diarisation is the layer it most needs and could most clearly win.
en.AI_OPPORTUNITY_2: (My judgement) Turn action items into sourced, signed tasks and track them to completion — extending from meeting notes to meeting execution, the one direction that raises ARPU without offending individual users.
en.ASSUMPTIONS_ONE_PARAGRAPH_LIST_WHAT_IS_I: Verifiable: site positioning and feature list, bot-free and compliance badges, 'Used at 500K+ companies' (site wording), five-tier pricing and feature mapping (USD list prices), the 2026-04-15 Superhuman acquisition announcement, the PH count of 316 reviews plus 8 latest excerpts, G2 4.6/177 with rating distribution, Fireflies' four-tier list prices, and the hands-on (RanBing) six-dimension record. Inferred and flagged: frequency, north-star and input/guardrail metrics, margin and unit cost, post-acquisition integration direction, and Granola/Otter prices (no quotable body text captured this round).
en.ASSUMPTION_1: [inferred] 'Used at 500K+ companies' counts companies, not paid seats, and includes free users; no user count, paid count or retention is disclosed, so any ARR derived from it is unreliable.
en.ASSUMPTION_2: [inferred] The paying core is team tiers, not individuals: the free plan already includes unlimited recording and transcription (pricing page), the hands-on run found free sufficient for an individual, and reviews document downgrades from Pro. Its growth curve therefore depends on when one person pulls a colleague in.
en.CATEGORY_POSITIONING_PARAGRAPH: It sits where two shelves cross: meeting notetakers (Fireflies, Otter, Granola) and sales/revenue intelligence (Gong). It leans toward recording but further toward action and integration — more CRM sync and Scorecards than a pure notetaker, less call scoring and methodology depth than Gong, more cross-meeting retrieval and open interfaces than platform-native tools.
en.CURRENT_AI_USAGE_PARAGRAPH: AI appears in six places: ASR transcription with diarisation, instant summaries, AI action items and follow-up email, Trackers (continuous topic monitoring), Ask Fathom (cross-meeting Q&A), and AI Scorecards plus CRM field extraction; externally, a public API and MCP for other AIs. The hands-on run used only the most basic slice — record, summarise, extract actions — and it already held up.
en.FINAL_BREAKS: Heavy Chinese-language meetings needing high accuracy (the hands-on barrier verdict); customers who won't allow a third party in the room (a bot joining is the only capture objection named in Cons); industries requiring on-prem or data that never leaves the intranet; enterprises needing room hardware and in-person audio capture.
en.FINAL_MOAT_OR_LACK_THEREOF: The moat is weak-to-moderate: only three real moats, all coverable — free-tier thickness (subsidies can match it), bot-free capture (Granola already does it), and meeting-data accumulation plus exits (void the day platforms open export). Its actual asset is the 'individuals get fluent, teams pay' path and seven comparison pages of search real estate — not the model.
en.FINAL_WINS: A free tier thick enough to erase trial friction, bot-free capture that removes in-meeting social friction, cross-meeting retrieval and MCP that make it someone else's data source, and seven competitor comparison pages forming a high-intent SEO matrix.
en.SIX_INTRO: Written along the six application-layer dimensions: not how many AI features it has, but which step it replaces and which trouble it hands back. Evidence: the 20-minute hands-on run on 2026-11-19 (RanBing), site and pricing copy, and reviews captured from Product Hunt and G2.
en.AI_TYPE_REASON: Unplug test: remove ASR and summarisation and only audio plus calendar entries remain — it can record but not read, degrading to a voice recorder. So it is AI-native, not embedded. But native in two halves: a recording shell and an AI brain, with judgement on the AI side (hands-on: 'one part is meeting recording, one part is AI recognition and context judgement').
en.SIX_1: It replaces the 'write the notes and email them round' step: a human used to spend at least half an hour, and meeting content never turned into actions directly. Now feedback is captured during the meeting and the summary plus action items exist afterwards (hands-on: 'it used to be manual; now I can capture feedback during the meeting — before it took at least half an hour'). Cost moves from labour to $0 entry, which is why the hands-on verdict was 'worth it'.
en.SIX_2: It eats transcription, summarisation, action items, follow-up email and CRM write-back; it hands back one thing — you must authorise and connect the meeting tools you actually use (hands-on: 'she needed me to connect the meeting tools I use'), and a human must confirm action items. That authorisation isn't laziness, it's the category's entry fee: no meeting, no audio.
en.SIX_3: Directly usable. Hands-on: 'usable as-is; what needs editing is the meeting consensus and the action list.' In team settings people do send it out as-is (she pushes it for team use). So what comes back is signable notes, not a draft needing reformatting.
en.SIX_4: Thin safety net: it faithfully records and reports per meeting, with no source attribution and no confidence level; give it a wrong premise and it follows it (hands-on: 'if the premise you give it is wrong, she follows along too — the fallback is human confirmation'). The only real fallback is a person.
en.SIX_5: You can't afford to be wrong. History and replay exist (reversible), but in a meeting where sales decisions form live, a miswritten action item bends everything downstream — and the commitment has already been spoken, so it's irreversible (hands-on: 'in something where you're forming a sales decision while talking, you can't afford to be wrong').
en.SIX_6: Replaceable for an individual, not for a team. Hands-on: 'replaceable — other free meeting recorders can substitute, but they differ in recognition stability; teams with tight timing and close demands can't switch, and the free version gets better the more you use it.' So retention isn't 'can't leave' — it's 'no reason to leave'.

extra_zh.title: 对标竞品地图
extra_zh.body:
缺件先说：Product Hunt 产品页本次被 Cloudflare 拦截，只拿到评论计数（316）与 8 条最新原话，没拿到 More alternatives 栏目，所以这张地图的名单不来自 PH，而来自三处——官网 Competitors 导航（它自己列了七个对手）、官方 Solutions 里正面撞上的销售智能层，以及评论里用户说实际换去的地方。

谁抢同一个需求抢同一段链路用户实际迁移
Fireflies.ai会议多、要纪要的销售与团队bot 入会 + 转写 + 摘要 + 助手（AskFred）最直接的同类：官网自述 1,000,000+ companies，100+ 语言，年付 10 美元起——比它便宜、语种比它多，是它价格侧最硬的对手
Granola不想让机器人进会的个人与小组本地系统音频 + 无 bot + 摘要抢的正是它的 bot-free 卖点，且更彻底（纯本地、Mac 优先）；本次定价页为 JS 渲染未读到正文，不做价格对比
Otter.ai会议 + 录音笔双场景的通用用户自研 ASR + OtterPilot 自动入会老牌通用型，教育与政企长尾深；对它的威胁在品牌默认值，不在功能
Gong销售管理者要的「通话里的收入信号」通话评分 + 销售方法 + 收入智能它的 Business 档（25 美元，含 Deal View 与 AI Scorecards）正好走进 Gong 的主场；往上打会被 Gong 的深度挡住，往下打会被 Fireflies 的价格挡住——这是它最窄的一段
Read AI / ZoomMate会议摘要 + 会议洞察bot 入会 + 摘要 + 会议分析同质化竞争，靠集成与免费档拉开；官网把它们列进对比页，等于承认这层没有技术壁垒
平台原生（Meet 的 Gemini / Teams 的 Copilot / Zoom AI Companion）所有已经在开会的人会议软件内直接记录与摘要最危险的一路：不用授权、不用装、不用请机器人，边际成本为零。它官网把 Gemini 写进 Competitors，是它自己承认的威胁

读法：它在地图上的位置很尴尬——下面被价格与语种压（Fireflies）、侧面被 bot-free 更彻底的产品切（Granola）、上面被销售智能的深度挡（Gong）、外面被平台原生免费盖（Gemini / Copilot）。它唯一的空位是「免费档 + 跨会议检索 + 开放接口」这个组合，而这个组合恰好是平台不愿意做、同类做不好的那一段。

extra_zh.title: 竞品技术底座
extra_zh.body:
产品底座会议到行动之间的接缝
Fathom第三方 ASR + 自建摘要与结构化抽取；bot 走会议平台 SDK 入会，bot-free 走桌面端系统音频采集；Public API 与 MCP 对外开放；CRM 走官方连接器（Salesforce / HubSpot）接缝在「会后」：摘要 → 行动项 → CRM 字段 → Slack/Notion/Asana。它把接缝做成了产品的一部分，而不是让用户自己搬
Fireflies.aibot 入会为主 + 自研/第三方混合 ASR + AskFred 检索；私有存储与区域化选项接缝在集成广度：几十个原生集成 + API，靠「接得上」赢
Granola桌面端本地音频 + 云端模型摘要，无 bot接缝在「会后整理给人看」这一段，刻意不做 CRM 与团队治理
Otter.ai自研 ASR（多年积累）+ OtterPilot 自动入会 + 会议与录音笔双入口接缝在「录音笔时代的存量」，靠硬件与合作渠道延伸
Gong通话采集 + 自研语义分析 + 收入智能模型 + CRM 双向深度集成接缝在「销售方法论落地」：不是记录，是评分与教练
平台原生（Gemini / Copilot / AI Companion）会议软件内部音频流直取 + 平台自有大模型 + 同一账号体系接缝被抹平：没有采集这一步，也就没有授权摩擦；代价是只在自家会议软件里成立

[推断] 真护城河不在 ASR 也不在摘要——这两层都已商品化，任何一家都能买到同等质量。真正难复制的三样是：①采集入口（bot 要过会议平台的接入与合规，bot-free 要做桌面端音频，两条都不轻松）；②会议数据沉淀（历史越多，检索越准，换工具的代价越高）；③集成深度（CRM 字段映射与回写规则是脏活，做一次不够，要一直跟着对方的 API 变更维护）。反过来说，它把 AI 做得越像「能写纪要」，越容易被平台原生替代；把自己做得越像「会议事实层」，越难被替代——MCP 这一步选的正是后者。

extra_zh.title: 可迁移的机会（我的判断）
extra_zh.body:
1. 把「先授权、后下载」做成标准 onboarding——注册 → 逐步授权 → 最后才装客户端，让第一次打开就有结果。实测（燃冰）记录的顺序就是这样，它把「空界面」这一关直接删掉了。任何需要连接外部数据源才有价值的 AI 产品，都该抄这个顺序；反过来，先装客户端再要授权，等于让用户先面对一个空壳。最轻，改流程不改架构。
  2. 把「AI 起草、人签字」做成显式的确认步——行动项标来源时间戳与说话人，确认后才进 CRM 或发给客户，未确认的留草稿。实测原话是它「提炼下一步行动然后让人确认」，这个设计是对的；但确认这一步在产品里还不够显眼，而它错一次的代价是承诺写错。最值，因为它直接换信任。
  3. 用「无限」而不是「限量」做免费档——它的免费档给无限录制与转写，换来的是 316 条评论里只有 10 条抱怨。对任何按用量计成本的产品，这是个反直觉但有效的选择：用功能设墙（团队协作、合规、集成），不用配额设墙——配额墙会让人在还没感受到价值时就开始算钱。
  4. 把对比页做成产品的一部分——七个对手七张对比页，专吃「X vs 我」的搜索。这不是市场部的事，是产品定位的事：能把每个对手的差异写清楚，说明自己知道自己在卖什么。最慢，但复利最长。

四个里哪个最该先做？第 2 个：它不增加功能，只把「谁负责」写清楚，而这类产品的全部风险都在「纪要写错了谁担」。哪个最容易被忽略？第 3 个——大多数团队第一反应是加限额，因为财务上更安全，但增长上更慢。

extra_zh.title: 流量与变现拆解
extra_zh.body:
钱从三方出：个人（Premium 16 美元）、团队（Team 15 / Business 25，每人每月）、企业（Enterprise 35，仅年付）。真正的现金流不看个人——免费档已经无限录制与转写，个人几乎不需要付费；收入跳变发生在「一个人把同事拉进共享工作区」那一刻。

环节它怎么做的为什么有效 / 哪里漏
拉新免费档 + 七张竞品对比页 + 集成目录（Salesforce、HubSpot、Slack、Asana、Zapier、ChatGPT、Claude）有效：试用零成本，搜索意图极准。漏点：平台原生免费，用户根本不会来搜「替代品」
激活注册 → 授权 → 下载 → 进会 → 出摘要有效：第一次打开就有结果。漏点：授权这一步要交出会议入口，是全程唯一会让用户犹豫的地方
留存历史会议可搜 + Trackers + CRM 回写有效：会议档案越厚越难走。漏点：个人层的留存不等于付费留存，很多人在免费档就满足了
变现个人 16 / 团队 15–35 每人每月，年付省 25%+，90 天保证有效：团队与合规是硬需求。漏点：价差只有 15 → 25 → 35，跨度太窄，每档必须绑一项「组织才需要」的能力，否则升级没动力
扩张席位随团队人数增长；Business 加 CRM 同步与教练指标；Enterprise 加 SSO/SCIM、自定义留存、自定义 BAA[推断] 扩张的主要阻力不是价格，是采购流程：SSO 与 BAA 一旦是硬要求，决策周期会从「一个人点一下」变成「IT 与法务排队」

一句话：它的漏斗设计得很干净，问题在漏斗的出口——免费档太好，个人没有付费理由；平台原生太近，团队没有换的理由。它的解法只有一个，而且已经在做：把自己变成「会议事实层」，让别人的 AI 来读（API / MCP），这样它就不必和会议软件争同一块屏幕。

extra_en.body:
Missing piece first: the Product Hunt listing was blocked by Cloudflare this round, so only the review count (316) and 8 latest excerpts were captured — the More alternatives block was not obtained. This map therefore does not use PH; its names come from three places: the site's own Competitors menu (seven rivals), the sales-intelligence layer its Business tier collides with, and the substitutes reviewers say they actually moved to.

WhoSame needSame link in the chainWhere users actually go

Reading it: the position is awkward — squeezed from below on price and languages (Fireflies), cut from the side by more thorough bot-free products (Granola), blocked from above by sales-intelligence depth (Gong), and covered from outside by free native capture (Gemini / Copilot). Its only open slot is the combination of a generous free tier, cross-meeting retrieval and open interfaces — exactly what platforms won't build and peers can't build well.

extra_en.title: Competitors' technical base
extra_en.body:
ProductBaseThe seam between meeting and action
FathomThird-party ASR plus in-house summarisation and structured extraction; a bot joins via meeting-platform SDKs, bot-free captures desktop system audio; public API and MCP; CRM via official connectors (Salesforce / HubSpot)The seam is after the meeting: summary → action items → CRM fields → Slack/Notion/Asana. It made the seam part of the product instead of making users carry it
Fireflies.aiBot-first, hybrid ASR, AskFred retrieval; private storage and regional optionsThe seam is integration breadth: dozens of native integrations plus API — it wins by connecting
GranolaDesktop local audio plus cloud-model summaries, no botThe seam is 'turn the meeting into something readable', deliberately skipping CRM and team governance
Otter.aiYears of in-house ASR, OtterPilot auto-join, meetings plus voice-recorder entry pointsThe seam is the recorder-era installed base, extended through hardware and partnerships
GongCall capture plus in-house semantic analysis plus revenue models plus deep two-way CRM integrationThe seam is putting sales methodology into practice: not recording, but scoring and coaching
Platform-native (Gemini / Copilot / AI Companion)Direct audio from the meeting app plus the platform's own models plus one account systemThe seam disappears: no capture step means no permission friction — at the cost of working only inside its own meeting app

[inferred] The real moat is neither ASR nor summarisation — both are commoditised and anyone can buy equal quality. The three hard-to-copy things are: (1) capture entry (a bot must clear meeting-platform access and compliance; bot-free means building desktop audio — neither is easy); (2) meeting-data accumulation (more history means better retrieval and a higher cost to leave); (3) integration depth (CRM field mapping and write-back rules are dirty work that never ends, because the other side's API keeps changing). The more it looks like 'AI that writes notes', the more replaceable by native tools; the more it looks like the 'meeting source of truth', the harder to replace — and MCP picks the latter.

extra_en.title: Transferable opportunities (my judgement)
extra_en.body:
1. Turn 'authorise first, download last' into standard onboarding — signup → stepwise permissions → install only at the end, so the first launch already has results. That is the sequence the hands-on run recorded, and it deletes the empty-screen moment. Any AI product that only becomes valuable once an external source is connected should copy this order; installing a client before asking for permissions forces the user to stare at a shell. Lightest: a process change, not an architecture change.
  2. Make 'AI drafts, human signs' an explicit confirmation step — each action item carries its source timestamp and speaker; nothing enters the CRM or reaches a client until confirmed, and unconfirmed items stay drafts. The hands-on line is that it extracts next actions and has a human confirm them — the right design, but the confirmation step is not prominent enough in the product, and one wrong commitment is the failure mode that matters. Most valuable, because it buys trust directly.
  3. Meter the free tier by features, not by quota — unlimited recording and transcription produced only 10 complaints across 316 reviews. For any product with per-use inference cost this is counter-intuitive but effective: put the wall on team collaboration, compliance and integrations rather than on minutes, because a quota wall makes people count money before they feel value.
  4. Make comparison pages part of the product — seven rivals, seven pages, eating 'X vs us' searches. This is positioning work, not marketing work: stating each rival's difference precisely proves you know what you sell. Slowest, longest compounding.

Which first? Number 2 — it adds no features, only clarity about who is accountable, and accountability is where this category's entire risk sits. Which gets ignored? Number 3 — most teams reach for a quota because it is safer financially, and slower for growth.

extra_en.title: Traffic and monetisation breakdown
extra_en.body:
Money comes from three places: individuals (Premium $16), teams (Team $15 / Business $25 per user per month) and enterprise (Enterprise $35, annual only). Cash flow doesn't really come from individuals — free already includes unlimited recording and transcription — the step change happens when one person pulls a colleague into a shared workspace.

StageWhat it doesWhy it works / where it leaks
AcquisitionFree tier + seven competitor comparison pages + integration directories (Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack, Asana, Zapier, ChatGPT, Claude)Works: zero-cost trial, high-intent search. Leak: native is free, so many users never search for an 'alternative' at all
ActivationSignup → permissions → download → join → summaryWorks: the first launch already has a result. Leak: the permission step asks for the meeting entry point — the only place users hesitate
RetentionSearchable meeting history + Trackers + CRM write-backWorks: the thicker the archive, the harder to leave. Leak: individual retention isn't paid retention — many are satisfied on free
Monetisation$16 individual / $15–35 per seat for teams, 25%+ off annual, 90-day guaranteeWorks: teams and compliance are hard requirements. Leak: the ladder is only 15 → 25 → 35, so each step must carry something only an organisation needs, or nobody climbs
ExpansionSeats grow with headcount; Business adds CRM sync and coaching metrics; Enterprise adds SSO/SCIM, custom retention, custom BAA[inferred] The brake isn't price but procurement: the moment SSO and a BAA become mandatory, the cycle goes from one click to IT and legal queueing

One line: the funnel is cleanly designed; the exit is the problem — free is too good, so individuals have no reason to pay; native is too close, so teams have no reason to switch. It has exactly one answer, and is already executing it: become the meeting source of truth that other AIs read through API and MCP, so it no longer fights the meeting app for the same screen.
